scenarios.heading: Five patterns that clear verification and still cost you money
scenarios.sub: For each: how it works, why current systems miss it, how Shruhani catches it — and what it measured in production.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[0].description: A mule account is opened with genuine documents by a real person, recruited for ₹5,000 to ₹30,000 to lend their identity. It clears every KYC check, stays dormant, then activates as a pass-through for stolen funds.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[0].title: Modus operandi
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[1].description: KYC confirms the identity is authentic, not why the account is being opened. Bureau returns no negative history, so detection happens only after the money has moved.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[1].title: Why current systems miss it
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[2].description: Shruhani reads the digital and behavioural profile at account opening — recently activated phone, minimal footprint, shared device, coached session. Individually flags; together, a conviction.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[2].title: How Shruhani catches it
scenarios.tabs[0].label: Mule accounts
scenarios.tabs[0].proofBody: of money mules flagged at onboarding — 3× better than the legacy system it replaced.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[0].description: A fabricated persona assembled from real fragments: valid Aadhaar, fresh phone, new email, clean selfie. No negative history, because the person never existed. Sophisticated variants warm up with small transactions first.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[0].title: Modus operandi
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[1].description: Each document is individually valid. Bureau returns nothing, and absence of history reads as absence of risk. The identity passes because there is nothing to fail against.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[1].title: Why current systems miss it
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[2].description: Digital Footprint tests whether the identifiers belong to a person with an established presence. A genuine identity leaves years of traces across 100+ platforms. A synthetic one does not.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[2].title: How Shruhani catches it
scenarios.tabs[1].label: Synthetic identity
scenarios.tabs[1].proofBody: of fraudsters concentrated in the riskiest 5% of applicants scored.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[0].description: An unauthorised party takes control of a legitimate account using valid credentials from phishing, social engineering, or a SIM swap. The login succeeds. The session behaviour changes.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[0].title: Modus operandi
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[1].description: Authentication verifies credentials, not the person using them. Once the login succeeds, the session is treated as legitimate for its full duration.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[1].title: Why current systems miss it
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[2].description: Behavioural Biometrics baselines how each holder interacts with their device and scores deviation in real time — inside the session, not after the transfer clears.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[2].title: How Shruhani catches it
scenarios.tabs[2].label: Account takeover
scenarios.tabs[2].proofBody: from session deviation to block on takeover attempts in production.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[0].description: A coordinated network of accounts run by a handful of people or devices. Every account passes individual verification; the coordination shows only across the network — shared devices, clustered IPs, linked funding.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[0].title: Modus operandi
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[1].description: Per-account scoring treats each application as independent. One account inside a 200-account ring looks ordinary. The ring is invisible to any system evaluating one at a time.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[1].title: Why current systems miss it
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[2].description: Shruhani maps relationships across accounts, devices, numbers and funding paths continuously. The ring surfaces not because one account is suspicious, but because the connections are.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[2].title: How Shruhani catches it
scenarios.tabs[3].label: Fraud rings
scenarios.tabs[3].proofBody: distinct fraud rings surfaced from 69,646 numbers; one device operating 150 accounts.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[0].description: In Tier 2/3 markets, agents fill forms, operate devices and take selfies for applicants. The KYC documents are genuine. The person completing the application is not the applicant.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[0].title: Modus operandi
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[1].description: Face match confirms the selfie matches the Aadhaar and liveness confirms a real person. Neither confirms the person holding the device is the applicant.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[1].title: Why current systems miss it
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[2].description: Image Intelligence reads background scene, device metadata and Face Vault history; Behavioural Biometrics detects coached capture. Right documents, wrong behavioural signature.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[2].title: How Shruhani catches it
scenarios.tabs[4].label: Agent-driven fraud
scenarios.tabs[4].proofBody: of approved selfies flagged as assisted captures; 1,400+ duplicate identity clusters found.

seo.metaDescription: Stop identity fraud, mule accounts and fraud rings in real time. Shruhani unifies device, behavioural and digital footprint signals into one AI risk score.
split.body:
Indian financial fraud has undergone a structural shift. The era of forged documents and impersonated identities is being replaced by a more sophisticated pattern: fraud committed with genuine credentials. Synthetic identities are assembled from valid fragments. Mule accounts are opened with fully compliant KYC. Account takeovers are executed with legitimate login credentials. In each case, the verification infrastructure confirms the identity. What it does not confirm, and was never built to confirm, is the intent behind it.
The result is a category of loss that traditional fraud systems are architecturally unable to prevent. Not because they are poorly configured, but because they answer a question that no longer separates legitimate customers from fraudulent ones.
